newsitem.title: USA: KCBT WHEAT ENDS UP ON TECHNICALS, SUPPLY CONCERNS.
newsitem.headline: KCBT WHEAT ENDS UP ON TECHNICALS, SUPPLY CONCERNS.

text.p: KCBT hard red winter wheat futures settled firmer on spillover strength from outside markets, but traders said futures also drew support from concern over crop prospects in other parts of the globe.

Wheat gained in conjunction with a surprising rally in CBOT corn and soybeans, which had been called to open lower on bearish crop estimates by Conrad Leslie-ADM. Wheat also saw technical strength, which befuddled some market players.
"Everything was a stretch here. Fundamental traders are still trying to come up with reasons to explain why we're higher," a KCBT trader said.

Traders said wheat may have been buoyed by ongoing rumors of an Egyptian purchase and by concerns over weather problems affecting the Australian and Canadian crops. Traders also cited possible quality problems with the French crop.
"There's been talk coming out of Europe about low falling numbers in the French crop," a KCBT trader said.
KCBT wheat settled three to four cents per bushel higher, with September up four cents at $3.80.
The KCBT estimated Friday's volume at 31.67 million bushels, which would be well below Thursday's actual volume of 48.145 million bushels.
Featured players included ADM's Benson-Quinn, which bought 1.5 million December bushels but also sold one million Dec. FIMAT bought 1.5 million Dec and sold 1.5 million Sept.
